builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DPMA: Learning to Compress Mixture-of-Experts Models
summary: DPMA replaces heuristic, uniform-ratio expert pruning or merging in retraining-free MoE compression with jointly learned prune/merge/absorb decisions and per-layer expert allocation under a global budget. It costs a gradient-based optimization pass over calibration data with the base weights frozen, plus the complexity of routing-weight redirection, rather than any retraining of the model itself. It can fail when calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, when only multiple-choice benchmark gains transfer poorly to generative workloads, or when the retained expert set degrades capability for rare inputs previously handled by removed experts.
rationale: DPMA can shrink MoE memory footprint substantially with frozen weights and modest calibration compute, but its gradient-based compression search and dependence on calibration data require validation on the reader's specific model and workload before production use.
technique: Learned MoE expert pruning, merging, and routing absorption

claims.statement: DPMA replaces heuristic, uniform-ratio expert pruning or merging in retraining-free MoE compression with jointly learned prune/merge/absorb decisions and per-layer expert allocation under a global budget. It costs a gradient-based optimization pass over calibration data with the base weights frozen, plus the complexity of routing-weight redirection, rather than any retraining of the model itself. It can fail when calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, when only multiple-choice benchmark gains transfer poorly to generative workloads, or when the retained expert set degrades capability for rare inputs previously handled by removed experts.

At 75% expert reduction, DPMA outperforms the strongest baseline on all four evaluated MoE models, with accuracy gains of up to 6.7 percentage points; it achieves the highest accuracy averaged over benchmarks and compression ratios on each model.
